name: Acacias — savanna thorn trees and Australian wattles
status: 5 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: The trees that make a savanna read as savanna: flat-topped umbrella thorns, fever trees along pans, whistling thorns with their ants, camel thorn in the Kalahari, babul and cutch in India, mulga, brigalow and gidgee across Australia, huisache and catclaw in the Americas. Savanna biomes should be dominated by these at low density with grass between — never a closed canopy.

canopy.name: Umbrella thorn
canopy.origin: Africa (Sahel to South Africa) and Arabia

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two oval cotyledons, then tiny feathery bipinnate leaves on a thin stem with paired spines, some long, straight and white, others short and hooked. The taproot dives deep first. Browsed saplings become dense, low, cage-like spiny bushes for years; once a leader escapes browsers it gains about 1.5 m in two years and only later spreads the flat umbrella crown.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (Acacia tortilis): up to 21 m, about 1.5 m in 2 years, a 6-7-year-old tree yields 5-6 kg of clean seed, 10-12 kg pods a year at 10 yr; Andersen & Krzywinski 2007 (BMC Ecology): radiocarbon ages of 200-650 yr for trees in Egypt's Eastern Desert, radial growth up to 2.4 mm a year. Germination and height curve estimated.

canopy.source: Sahel to South Africa savanna; the flat-top. Kew POWO (African acacias are now Vachellia/Senegalia; Acacia is the Australian wattles). Thorny (African), flat crowns, insect-pollinated, pods eaten by browsers which spread the seed; giraffe and goat browse; fire-adapted.

Flowering at the onset of the rains, ripening, pod fall and rot times estimated.

canopy.name: Fever tree

growth.juvenile_note: Hot-water-soaked seed sprouts quickly; seedlings have two oval cotyledons, reach the two-leaf stage in 6-8 weeks and carry feathery bipinnate leaves and pairs of straight white spines. Young trees shoot up 1-1.5 m a year as slender single-stemmed whips, and the powdery greenish-yellow bark that names the tree shows early; the flat-topped crown spreads later.
growth.source: SANBI PlantZAfrica (Vachellia xanthophloea): 15-25 m, about 1.5 m a year under ideal conditions, seed soaked overnight in hot water, two-leaf stage 6-8 weeks after sowing, dappled shade below; ICRAF Agroforestree: 1-1.5 m a year. First flowering, lifespan and height curve estimated.

canopy.name: Camel thorn

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal, with two thick oval cotyledons and grey-green feathery bipinnate leaves on a zigzag stem armed with pairs of large, swollen-based, white spines. The seedling pours its effort into a taproot that heads down toward groundwater (in old trees it may reach tens of metres) while the shoot grows slowly, so young plants are sparse, very spiny, grey-green bushes for years.
growth.source: SANBI PlantZAfrica (Vachellia erioloba): 2 m shrub to 16 m tree, slow-growing, starts flowering at about 10 years, seeds take 4-6 weeks to germinate after a boiling-water soak, taproot can reach 60 m; ICRAF Agroforestree: flowers at about 10 yr, regular pod crops by 20 yr, crown to 18 m. Height curve and lifespan estimated.

canopy.name: Mulga

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: 2 cotyledons, then a few feathery bipinnate true leaves before narrow silvery-grey phyllodes take over in the first months. It sends a taproot ~3 m down while only 20 cm tall and stays a slender silver sprig for years (20 cm at 6-8 months), then becomes a many-stemmed shrub whose branches angle upward like a funnel.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree DB and Winrock FACT sheet (germinates in ~10 days after scarification; 20 cm at 6-8 months; 3 m multi-stemmed shrub at 10 yr on 370 mm rain); Hawaii PRA (reproductive maturity 10+ yr); The Conversation 2019 (lives three centuries or more; 3 m taproot at 20 cm tall)

shrub.name: Whistling thorn

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two oval cotyledons and small feathery bipinnate leaves on a wiry stem armed with paired straight white spines. Saplings in the black-clay grasslands are browsed and burned back, staying spiny multi-stemmed bushes for years; then they start making swollen hollow thorn bases (bulbs, soft and green at first, hardening purple-black, then grey) that ants move into.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Vachellia drepanolobium): up to 6 m, on East African black-cotton soils, hollow swollen thorns housing Crematogaster and Tetraponera ants (C. mimosae on about half the trees). Germination, growth, first flowering and lifespan estimated from related East African savanna acacias.
